description: The second run ranges from Greek mythology and maritime mystery to aviation, mountaineering, northern European geography, Monopoly, vocabulary and surveying, with each subject offering a fresh way to turn recognition into uncertainty.

s02e01.description: The Wicked Witch, Cruella de Vil, Darth Vader and Voldemort are put into chronological order before questions turn to mushy peas, rugby tries, the Red Arrows, SPF and Frank Sinatra. Greek mythology later supplies the Queen of the Underworld.

s02e02.description: A booby prize, a barn owl, A Star Is Born, a National Lottery Thunderball game, party whips and the earliest possible Easter month all appear in the same broadcast. Maritime mystery then takes over with the famously abandoned Mary Celeste.

s02e03.description: George VI, Twilight’s Edward Cullen, the atomic nucleus, the Thrilla in Manila and Cate Blanchett playing Katharine Hepburn all make appearances. The odd trio of Dallas, Brett and Kane provides the episode with its most wonderfully specific piece of trivia.

s02e04.description: The Little Mermaid statue and Hans Christian Andersen, cartography, Love Island narrator Iain Stirling and Citizen Kane’s Charles Foster Kane all feature before the questions head outdoors for the Three Peaks Challenge.

s02e05.description: Steve Smith and cricket’s ball-tampering scandal share space with famous spectacle-wearers, Halloween and badminton. The geographical high point is considerably colder: the paired Scandinavian waterways Skagerrak and Kattegat.

s02e06.description: Montreal and Quebec, Liberal leader Jeremy Thorpe and Jack Vettriano’s The Singing Butler all turn up before a familiar board game becomes unexpectedly exacting. London Monopoly properties provide the episode’s wonderfully specific map of trivia.

s02e07.description: Pixar films are put in release order before the ladder visits dawn, the Cabinet, Prue Leith, Cambodia and spicy food. Natural history later introduces the condor, giving the episode a suitably large-winged answer among a very mixed flock of subjects.

s02e08.description: Diapers, Canary Wharf, Maid Marian, origami, the Mona Lisa and the suspiciously light table-tennis ball all appear in quick succession. Aerodynamics eventually contributes the Gurney flap, exactly the sort of tiny technical object Millionaire loves to make suddenly important.

s02e09.description: String instruments, chips, ballerina tutus, the port side of a ship, Mumbai and radiator keys all precede Lady Godiva’s famous ride through Coventry. Few quiz ladders travel from household plumbing to naked horseback history quite so efficiently.

s02e10.description: Tour de France winner Geraint Thomas and Deadpool’s alter ego Wade Wilson sit on either side of a vocabulary question about the meaning of quotidian. Sport, language and superheroes make for a compact but unusually memorable mixture.

s02e11.description: Cluedo, white lies, Noah’s Ark, oyster pearls, carbon dioxide, rower Matthew Pinsent and lexicography all appear before surveying equipment gets its turn. The theodolite is the sort of object most people recognise right up until they have to name it.
